Hello calibration leads —

Thanks for carving time this week. Goal: ship a clean calibration outcome for Q2 by EOD Friday that minimizes exceptions and gives clear rationale for the handful of split-band cases. A few asks up front so the live session is efficient: 

- Please review the attached calibration_matrix_v2.xlsx and the "split_band" tab before the session.
- Flag up to 3 contested cases per manager (highlight in the sheet) and prepare the 1–2 strongest pieces of evidence (project impact, objective metrics, peer feedback).
- For any cross-regional comparators, add a short note in the comments column describing population differences.

Quick framing: we've seen more "anchoring" where an evaluator's previous year's rating or a single project is overweighting the overall signal. During the session we'll adopt a simple decision tree (see link) intended to preserve manager judgment but require stronger evidence for upward adjustments that cross a band boundary.

Links: calibration matrix -> https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-calibration-matrix-v2
Appeals/exception process -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HR/pages/appeals-playbook

Prep deadline: EOD Wednesday (2026-05-13) so I can consolidate notes. We will meet Thursday 10:30–12:00 PT.

Thanks —
Michael
Michael Grant

Thanks Michael — will do. Quick question: one of my managers (Tom Jensen, client-eng) has a direct where peer and skip scores are split across bands (two evaluators put the person in high band, one in low).

What should the default tie-breaker be in that scenario? Will managers be allowed to make a final case, or are we escalating all >1-evaluator splits to HR? I know you mentioned evidence strength, but we should codify the gating so managers know what to bring.

I can attach a short packet for Tom's case if that helps.

—Marissa
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluator anchoring & split-band resolution: calibration kickoff

Marissa —

I took a pass through the split_band tab and added a couple of notes. Suggestion for the tie-breaker logic we can adopt in the session:

- If evaluators are split across adjacent bands (e.g., band 2 vs band 3) with a 2:1 vote, default to the median/evaluator average after normalizing by evaluator leniency (percentile-corrected within role).
- If the split crosses two or more bands or there's a 1:1:1 type split, require manager evidence (metrics + manager-collected peer anecdotes) and a short "case doc" (<=1 page).
- Upward adjustments that move a direct >1 band need VP sign-off and HR notification; downward movements should be documented and reviewed by the manager's skip-level.

I've added a simple percentile normalization column in the sheet (column G) — it's primitive but helps see whether one evaluator is an outlier. Happy to walk through the formula during the session.

-Laura
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 14:45:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluator anchoring & split-band resolution: calibration kickoff

Appreciate the clarity Laura — this matches my intent. To make execution simple in the live session, let's formalize a 4-step decision tree (I'll paste here so folks have it):

1) Adjacent-band 2:1 split -> apply evaluator-normalized median; manager may present one piece of additional objective evidence (OK for rebuttal) but no automatic band move.
2) Non-adjacent split or 1:1 split -> require manager case doc (<=1 page) and bring to VC for discussion; if manager case moves a person up >1 band, VP sign-off required.
3) Clear outlier evaluator -> if one evaluator's percentile is >25 points away from cohort median, mark as 'evaluator-anchor' and require at least one corroborating data point (peer feedback, OKR delta, production metrics).
4) Appeals window -> HR will keep appeals_log_202605.csv; appeals accepted only on procedural grounds (process error) or fresh evidence not previously considered; no ad-hoc reopens for sentiment.

I'll run the decision tree at the top of the session and we can mark any cases that need VP/HR follow-up. Marissa — please attach Tom Jensen's packet ahead of the meeting if you can.

-Michael

Can we confirm that any upward change >1 band will be held for VP review before HR completes salary adjustments? I want consistent downstream coordination with comp/total rewards.

-Vivek
